title: NoSQL by family: document, key-value, wide column, graph and time series

videos.script: A relational database answers any question, inside transactions, on one machine. The databases called NoSQL each gave up part of that on purpose. {{trade}} What they got back is what the last three lessons found hard: data spread across servers by a key, and copies kept by the database itself. {{partition}} So designing for them starts from the questions, not the tables. The box office asks five kinds of question, and each fits a different shape. {{shapes}} Holding a seat is one key that expires. In Redis it is one command, and two buyers can never both get it. {{redis}} A show's page is one document. Scans at the door are rows sorted inside a partition. Who went where is a walk through a graph. Sales per minute is a time series. {{families}} And every one of them is another database to back up, watch and keep in step. The last section is about when that is worth it. {{tax}}
